seo.title: eLearning Localization & Course Production | EPUBTRANS
seo.description: EPUBTRANS supports eLearning localization, course layout adaptation, multimedia integration and QA for supported Storyline, Rise and Lectora workflows.

hero.title: eLearning Localization Services
hero.lead: Multilingual course production, layout adaptation and localization support for training companies, localization service providers and learning-content teams.
paragraphs: Localization production for supported eLearning courses, including target-language content integration, layout adaptation and specified functional checks.

lead.text: Slides, interactive elements, quizzes, videos, navigation controls, audio and completion settings all contribute to the learner experience.

Translated text can change the space needed within buttons or text boxes. On-screen graphics may contain embedded text. Multimedia timing may need adjustment, while interactive elements and assessments must be reviewed within the localized course.
EPUBTRANS supports localization service providers, translation agencies and learning-content teams with the technical preparation and adaptation of eligible course materials.

blocks.text: Incorporating approved target-language content into supported eLearning authoring environments.
Depending on the project, tasks may include:

items: Integrating translated lesson text and headings
Updating buttons, labels and navigation text
Formatting feedback messages and assessment text
Addressing layout changes caused by translated content

blocks.text: The work is based on the translated material and production instructions supplied or agreed for the project.
Translation accuracy and linguistic approval are separate requirements unless specifically commissioned.
Adapting course layouts to accommodate changes in text length, fonts and language presentation.
This may involve resizing text areas, adjusting the placement of visual elements, updating slide layouts and reviewing content flow.
Languages with right-to-left direction or complex scripts may require additional assessment of the authoring tool, available fonts and presentation behavior.
eLearning courses may contain clickable objects, tabs, hotspots, branching activities and other interactive components.
When these elements contain localized text or supporting assets, production changes may be required.
Depending on the course and agreed scope, we can assess:

items: States and triggers affected by localized content

blocks.text: Complex programming modifications, new interaction development and substantial functional redesign are separately scoped activities.
Quizzes and knowledge checks may require more than replacing the question text.
Relevant production activities may include integrating translated questions, answer options, feedback messages, result-screen content and assessment-related labels.
Changes to scoring logic, branching rules, question banks or completion conditions should be reviewed and approved before implementation.
Some training courses contain screenshots, diagrams, illustrations and graphics with embedded text.
These elements may require replacement, editing or reconstruction before localized content can be displayed appropriately.
Work can include integrating translated graphic labels, adjusting visual layout and preparing updated assets where agreed.
The source artwork, editability, image rights and expected output affect the work required.
Multimedia elements may need to be adapted for the target language.
Depending on the project, production can involve integrating supplied voiceover files, subtitles, captions, revised scripts or localized video assets.
Audio recording, voice talent, translation, subtitle creation, video editing and narration synchronization must be identified separately when required.
Completed course content may need to be prepared for review, distribution or deployment.
Where supported and included in scope, this may involve publishing course output, preparing agreed packages and organizing the source files and associated assets.
The required package format and compatibility checks depend on the authoring tool and target learning environment.

lead.text: EPUBTRANS's documented service portfolio includes experience with selected eLearning authoring environments.
The availability of current versions, licenses, translation methods and publishing features must be confirmed for each project.

blocks.text: Articulate Storyline courses may contain slides, animations, interactive objects, quizzes, triggers, variables and branching content.
Localization production can involve adapting these elements while working within the supported project structure.
Relevant activities may include:

items: Adjusting slide layouts and text boxes
Preparing agreed review or published output

blocks.text: Storyline offers different translation and localization workflows depending on its version and project configuration.
The selected method must be reviewed before confirming compatibility or deliverables.
Rise courses use a responsive, block-based approach to digital learning content.
Localization may require updates to lessons, text blocks, interactive activities, media, labels and knowledge checks.
Depending on the course and available permissions, supported workflows may involve translated content integration, course duplication, localization features, review and publication.
The availability of editable course access, subscription features and applicable localization methods must be confirmed before production.
Lectora courses may include structured pages, actions, interactive elements, assessments and supporting media.
Localization-related production can involve managing translated course content, adjusting layouts and reviewing the resulting course structure.
Documented Lectora workflows may use translation exports and imports, with the exact file format and process dependent on the application version.
The project must be assessed for current compatibility, required access and publishing specifications.
Projects involving other authoring tools or existing course packages can be assessed individually.
Support for a particular application, proprietary source format, plugin or publishing environment should not be assumed without confirming the technical requirements.

sections.title: eLearning Production Support for Localization Agencies

lead.text: EPUBTRANS works with localization service providers and translation agencies that require specialist production assistance for multilingual learning content.
Our role can complement an agency's existing translation and project-management processes.

blocks.text: When approved translated content is supplied, EPUBTRANS can assess the work required to integrate it into supported authoring files and adapt the layouts.
This can help distinguish the linguistic phase from course-production activities.
Some projects require source review, content extraction or preparation of course assets before translation.
These tasks may be included where the authoring tool, source access and agreed workflow support them.
A localization project may involve translators, linguistic reviewers, course developers, media producers and client stakeholders.
The agreed scope should identify who is responsible for translation, language approval, production changes, functional testing and final acceptance.
Projects involving multiple target languages may require consistent version naming, common course specifications, reference materials and review instructions.
We can assess these requirements as part of the project plan.

lead.text: eLearning localization can involve several related services, but they are not automatically included in a single production assignment.

blocks.text: Translation, terminology management, cultural adaptation and linguistic quality assurance are defined separately from technical course production unless the project agreement includes them.
Subtitle translation, timed-text production and caption preparation may be required for videos or narrated content.
Supported formats, timing rules and final media integration must be confirmed.
Target-language voiceover can involve script preparation, voice talent, recording, audio editing and synchronization.
These activities require separate specifications for language, voice, timing, audio format and quality review.

Rewriting training objectives, redesigning learning scenarios, developing new assessments or creating substantially new interactions falls outside standard localization production unless explicitly commissioned.
This separation helps establish realistic deliverables and review responsibilities.

lead.text: The availability of editable course files and supporting assets is an important factor in eLearning localization.
Useful project inputs may include:

items: Original course project files or authorized authoring-tool access
A reference course or published preview
Approximate course volume and preferred schedule

groups.title: Editable Course Source vs Published Package

blocks.text: An editable course project generally provides different production options from a published web or LMS package.
A published package may not contain all the authoring information needed to make changes and republish the course.
Where only published content is available, we can review the feasibility of reconstruction or alternative preparation. Complete editability or reconstruction cannot be assumed.

lead.text: Final deliverables depend on the authoring environment, project files, technical specifications and agreed scope.

blocks.text: Updated, editable course projects in an agreed supported authoring format.
Published files or packages prepared for an agreed delivery environment, where supported and commissioned.
Localized or adapted text, images, audio-related files, subtitle assets and supporting production resources.
Course previews or review materials made available through the agreed workflow and supported systems.
Issue lists, correction logs or test summaries where the relevant review and reporting activities have been commissioned and completed.
The delivery specification should identify the format, version, language organization, naming convention and any included acceptance evidence.
We examine the available authoring files, published course reference, multimedia assets, interactive components and target-language requirements.
Technical dependencies and missing source materials are identified.
We clarify the localization workflow, approved language content, authoring-tool versions, course deliverables, multimedia requirements and review stages.
Any complex interactions, LMS testing, accessibility work or additional development tasks are separately identified.
The approved target-language material is integrated into the supported course environment.
Required layout and asset changes are performed according to the agreed specification.
Applicable visual and functional checks are conducted.
Issues involving text overflow, navigation, media, quizzes or interactions are reviewed according to the agreed testing responsibilities.
Approved corrections are incorporated through the defined review process.
The final source files, publish packages and supporting assets are prepared for the agreed handoff.

lead.text: Course localization quality requires attention to both presentation and behavior.
Depending on the project, relevant checks may include:

items: Review in agreed browsers or devices

blocks.text: Visual review examines whether translated content is displayed as intended and whether layout changes follow the approved design.
Functional review examines specified course behaviors, such as navigation, interactive objects, branching and assessment presentation.
The test scenarios and acceptance criteria should be defined in advance.
Linguistic review evaluates the meaning, accuracy, terminology and suitability of the translated language.
It is distinct from technical production QA and is included only when separately agreed.

lead.text: Learning management systems (LMSs) may require particular publishing packages and completion-tracking behavior.
Depending on the authoring tool and project, the requested output may involve a SCORM, xAPI, cmi5 or other supported distribution format.
These requirements should be established before course publication.

blocks.text: Where available and commissioned, the course may be published using the agreed authoring-tool settings.
The target package type, application version and output settings must be confirmed.
Successful publishing from an authoring tool does not automatically demonstrate that a localized course behaves correctly in every LMS.
When LMS testing is included, the test plan should identify the target system, package version, launch behavior, progress tracking, completion rules and assessment reporting requirements.
A localized course should be reviewed against the agreed functional requirements.
However, complete functional equivalence, SCORM/xAPI conformance and acceptance by a specific LMS should not be promised without the relevant testing and documented evidence.

lead.text: Accessible eLearning may require particular attention to navigation, reading order, visual content, captions, alternative text, keyboard interaction and compatibility with assistive technologies.
Localization can introduce additional issues involving language identification, reading direction, translated alternative text or changes to interactive elements.
Where accessibility is a project requirement, the relevant criteria, target technologies and evaluation responsibilities should be defined separately.
Localization and routine functional QA do not automatically establish WCAG or Section 508 conformance.
Explore Accessibility Services

sections.title: What Affects eLearning Localization Scope & Schedule?

blocks.text: Different applications, versions and licensing arrangements provide different localization and publishing capabilities.
Editable course projects, original media assets and appropriate application access can significantly affect production feasibility.
Interactive screens, branching scenarios, quizzes, variables, animations and embedded modules may require additional attention.
The number of target languages, language-specific typography and review requirements influence project planning.
Narration, subtitles, translated graphics and synchronized media may introduce additional production stages.
Requested devices, browsers, accessibility checks, LMS platforms, package formats and correction rounds influence the production effort.
We review these factors before confirming scope, costs or delivery schedules.

lead.text: eLearning localization may require other production activities depending on the source content and expected deliverables.

blocks.text: Multilingual layout and formatting for course handouts, workbooks, presentations and related documents.
Subtitle and timed-text production for training videos and other media.
Voiceover-related production for course narration and multilingual media.
Conversion of source audio or video content into written transcripts where required.
Accessibility-related preparation and remediation for supported learning documents and digital content.
These services may be commissioned independently or coordinated within an agreed project.

eLearning localization is the adaptation of digital learning content for a target language or audience. In addition to translated text, it may involve course layout, graphics, navigation, assessments, multimedia and delivery requirements.

groups.title: Can EPUBTRANS work with Articulate Storyline 360?

blocks.text: Storyline and Storyline 360 are part of EPUBTRANS's documented workflow experience. Current version compatibility, source-file access, licensing and deliverables must be confirmed for the project.

groups.title: Do you support Articulate Rise 360 localization?

blocks.text: Rise is included in EPUBTRANS's documented eLearning portfolio. Supported localization methods, course access, permissions and publishing requirements must be assessed for the current environment.
Lectora is a documented production environment. The exact Lectora version, translation-file workflow, editable project format and required output must be confirmed before production.

groups.title: Can EPUBTRANS work with translated content supplied by our agency?

blocks.text: Yes, the documented production scope includes integration and layout adaptation of supplied target-language content. Translation and linguistic approval can remain with the localization agency under the agreed workflow.

groups.title: Can you localize interactive quizzes and branching courses?

blocks.text: Interactive elements and assessments can be assessed as part of the localization scope. Triggers, states, variables, scoring logic and branching behavior may require additional technical review or programming work.

groups.title: Do you provide voiceover, subtitles and media localization?

blocks.text: These are documented related service areas that may be included when specifically agreed. Language availability, scripts, recording requirements, subtitle formats, audio synchronization and media deliverables must be confirmed.

groups.title: Can you localize a course if we only have a published SCORM package?

blocks.text: A published SCORM package may not provide sufficient editable content for ordinary localization. We can assess the source package and determine whether suitable reconstruction or another workflow is feasible.

groups.title: Do you provide SCORM or xAPI course packages?

blocks.text: Supported authoring tools may offer SCORM, xAPI or other publishing options. EPUBTRANS's current production and testing scope for the requested output must be confirmed before committing to a deliverable.

groups.title: Do you test the localized course in our LMS?

blocks.text: LMS testing can be assessed as a separately specified activity. The target LMS, access arrangements, test cases, completion rules and reporting requirements should be agreed in advance.

groups.title: Does eLearning localization include accessibility compliance?

blocks.text: Not automatically. Accessibility production and evaluation require an explicit specification, testing scope and acceptance criteria.

groups.title: What information do you need for an eLearning localization quote?

blocks.text: Please share a representative course, available editable project files, authoring tool and version, target languages, translation availability, multimedia requirements, approximate number of slides or modules, expected output package and preferred schedule.
